title: Inside the Dorsey band: arrangers and the Clambake Seven
summary: He learned from Dorsey, playing brushes in the Clambake Seven with Yank Lawson, with Jimmie Mundy, Paul Weston and Dean Kincaid writing for the band.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: And I opened with Tommy; we were doing the Raleigh Kool Show at the same time, and I learned a great deal from
Tommy Dorsey -- this band that we played in was all styles of music, not only the great pretty sounds, ballad band -- but we had Jimmie Mundie writing for us, a great writer and arranger.
Now, he had previously worked for who?
But his original work was with Hines in Chicago?
Oh, he wrote for everybody. And Jimmie Mundie, and for the pretty songs, we had Paul Wetstein.
Name some of those tunes, Cliff - can you remember any of them?
Yeah. People would like to know some of these great records that you made.
I made the Clambake Seven songs with Yank Lawson, and I can't name you any specific numbers.

But the Clambake Seven was part of that thing -- I was only with them for 7 or 8 months, now. But I learned a great deal from Tommy, I played a lot of brushes, and we played uptown music, we played downtown music. Dean Kincaid was writing for the band, Tommy had a ...
Dean Kincaid was the lead saxophone player.
He's living down in Florida, now, isn't he?
